questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 40. • Each correct answer will score one mark. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper. Which quantity is an SI base quantity?

A student takes measurements to determine the constant acceleration of a model car moving from rest in a straight line. The measured values with their absolute uncertainties are shown. measured quantity uncertainty value displacement 16.5m ± 0.1m time 15.0s ± 1.0s The student uses the equation s = 1at2 to calculate the acceleration of the car. What is the acceleration and its absolute uncertainty?

An aeroplane is moving at a constant speed in a straight line at an angle θ to the horizontal. Four forces act on the aeroplane: thrust force T, weight W, lift force L and resistive force R. L T R (cid:1) W Which two equations must be correct?

options.A: L = W cosθ and T = R + W sinθ
options.B: L = W sinθ and T = R + W cosθ
options.C: L = W cosθ and T = R – W sinθ
options.D: L = W sinθ and T = R – W cosθ

questions.questionText: What is the definition of acceleration?

options.A: the rate of change of displacement
options.B: the rate of change of kinetic energy
options.C: the rate of change of momentum
options.D: the rate of change of velocity

questions.questionText: An astronaut on the Moon, where there is no air resistance, throws a ball. The ball’s initial velocity has a vertical component of 8.00ms–1 and a horizontal component of 4.00ms–1, as shown. initial velocity path of ball 8.00 m s–1 4.00 m s–1 The acceleration of free fall on the Moon is 1.62ms–2. What is the speed of the ball 9.00s after being thrown?

Two blocks, of mass 0.20kg and 0.50kg, are connected by a light inextensible string that passes over a frictionless pulley. rough block, horizontal mass 0.20 kg surface pulley block, mass 0.50 kg The blocks are initially held stationary. The block of mass 0.20kg rests on a rough horizontal surface. The block of mass 0.50kg is suspended in air. Air resistance is negligible. When the blocks are released, they have an acceleration of magnitude 2.0ms–2. What is the magnitude of the frictional force between the block of mass 0.20kg and the rough surface?
A resultant force causes an object to accelerate. What is equal to the resultant force?

options.A: the acceleration of the object per unit mass
options.B: the change in kinetic energy of the object per unit time
options.C: the change in momentum of the object per unit time
options.D: the change in velocity of the object per unit time

questions.questionText: An object falls from a stationary helicopter and reaches terminal velocity. What happens to the acceleration of the object between leaving the helicopter and reaching terminal velocity?

Two balls, of masses m and 2m, travelling in a vacuum with initial velocities 2v and v respectively, collide with each other head-on, as shown. m 2v v 2m After the collision, the ball of mass m rebounds to the left with velocity v. What is the loss of kinetic energy in the collision?

options.A: 3 mv2 B 3 mv2 C 9 mv2 D 9 mv2

questions.questionText: A force F is applied at an angle of 45° to a door handle at a distance d from the pivot of the handle, as shown. d F 45(cid:2) pivot handle What is the moment of the force about the pivot? Fd

A couple consists of two forces, each of magnitude F, that act in opposite directions in the same plane. The perpendicular distance between the two forces is d. F d F What is the torque of the couple? Fd F

The diagram shows an experiment to determine the force exerted on a ball by a horizontal air flow. 30(cid:2) ball air flow The ball is suspended by a light string and weighs 0.15N. The deflection of the string from vertical is 30°. The ball is in equilibrium. What is the force on the ball from the air flow?

Two solid cylindrical objects X and Y are held fully submerged in a liquid, as shown. surface of liquid Y X The objects have the same volume. The density of the material of Y is twice the density of the material of X. Both objects are stationary. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The force due to the liquid acting on the top surface of X is greater than that acting on the top surface of Y.
options.B: The pressure difference due to the liquid between the top and bottom surfaces of X is the same as that for Y.
options.C: The upthrust acting on X is the same as the upthrust acting on Y.
options.D: The weight of X is the same as the weight of Y.

questions.questionText: An electric car travels at a constant speed of 70kmh–1 for 80km on a straight horizontal road and uses energy E from its battery. The total resistive force acting on the car is proportional to (speed)2. Assume that the electric motor is 100% efficient. How much energy is used from the battery when the car travels at a constant speed of 60kmh–1 for 80km on the straight horizontal road?
What is meant by the efficiency of a system?

options.A: the total energy input to the system divided by the useful energy output by the system
options.B: the useful energy output from the system divided by the energy wasted by the system
options.C: the useful energy output from the system divided by the total energy input to the system
options.D: the energy wasted by the system divided by the total energy input to the system

questions.questionText: A source of sound waves is moving at a constant speed directly towards a stationary observer. The sound waves have a speed of 340ms–1 and a frequency of 480Hz. The observer hears sound waves of frequency 650Hz. What is the speed of the source?

A student is investigating two electromagnetic waves, X and Y, in a vacuum. Wave X has a wavelength of 5.2 × 10–7m. Wave Y has a frequency of 9.4GHz. Which principal regions of the electromagnetic spectrum contain waves X and Y? X Y
A plane polarised light wave of intensity I is incident normally on a polarising filter. The initial intensity of the transmitted wave is 0.
What can explain how stationary waves are formed from progressive waves?
A pipe has a length of 2.0m. It is open at one end and closed at the other end.
A teacher is explaining diffraction to a group of students. Which piece of apparatus is most appropriate for the teacher to use to demonstrate diffraction?

Coherent light of constant wavelength is incident normally on a double slit. Interference fringes are formed on a screen that is a fixed distance from the double slit. The screen is parallel to the double slit. The separation of the slits is varied. Which graph best shows the variation with slit separation a of the spacing x of the interference fringes?

Light of wavelength 690nmpasses through a diffraction grating with 300 lines per mm, producing a series of bright spots (maxima) on a screen. screen diffraction grating What is the total number of bright spots that are produced?

A fine mist of oil droplets is sprayed into air. As the oil droplets leave the nozzle of the spraying device they can become electrically charged. What is not a possible value for the charge on an oil droplet?

In the circuit shown, a fixed resistor X is connected in series with a battery and a variable resistor. X The power dissipated in resistor X is 7.2W when a current of 3.0A passes through it. The variable resistor is adjusted so that the power dissipated in X increases by 50%. What is the new current in the circuit?

The potential difference across a metal wire is kept constant. The length l and the diameter d of the wire are both varied. The type of metal is kept the same. How is the current in the wire related to l and d?

options.A: It is directly proportional to l and inversely proportional to d.
options.B: It is directly proportional to l and inversely proportional to d2.
options.C: It is inversely proportional to l and directly proportional to d.
options.D: It is inversely proportional to l and directly proportional to d2.

questions.questionText: A student sets up a circuit. The circuit diagram shows how the positive and negative terminals of a voltmeter are connected to the circuit. The voltmeter has an initial reading that is positive. + – V Which changes, if any, in temperature and light intensity would cause the voltmeter reading to decrease? temperature light intensity
Some resistors and a battery of electromotive force (e.m.f.) E and negligible internal resistance are connected in series, as shown. E Which statement is correct?

options.A: The e.m.f. across each resistor equals the potential difference across the battery.
options.B: The potential difference across each resistor equals the e.m.f. E of the battery.
options.C: The sum of the e.m.f.s across the resistors equals the potential difference across the battery.
options.D: The sum of the potential differences across the resistors equals the e.m.f. E of the battery.

Two nuclides are different isotopes of the same element. Which statement about the nuclides is correct?

options.A: Neutral atoms of the nuclides have the same number of electrons.
options.B: Nuclei of the nuclides have different numbers of protons.
options.C: Nuclei of the nuclides have the same number of nucleons.
options.D: Nuclei of the nuclides have the same number of neutrons.
